subject: Spikes in 429s and tail latency — suspected quota/burst policy mismatch
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightline.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spikes in 429s and tail latency — urgent

Hi Laura,

Over the last 90 minutes our production integration is seeing a sharp rise in 429 responses and increased tail latency for generation requests. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% and p99 latency doubled. This started shortly after we turned on a heavier batching profile to handle morning traffic.

We rely on Redwood for predictable headroom; this is impacting user sessions. Can someone triage immediately? I've attached a very small log snippet (request ids and timestamps) and a short timeline.

Attached: brightline_request_log_snippet.txt (3KB)

Sam
Sam Torres
Platform Engineer, Brightline Health
sam.torres@brightline.io
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightline.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spikes in 429s and tail latency — urgent

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the snippet. We're investigating now. Initial notes/questions:

- Can you confirm whether the integration is using a single API key or multiple keys per service?
- Approx request distribution: % small requests vs % long-generation calls?

Preliminary look at metrics shows correlated 429 bursts aligned with Brightline's bursty morning ramp. Two likely causes we will check immediately:
1) rate-limiter window/burst policy mismatch (configured burst window smaller than expected, causing repeated token-bucket exhaustion under the new batching profile)
2) a global safety-valve that recently went tighter in the region and is tripping on sustained bursts

I'm looping in Karthik and Marissa to confirm config and request an emergency tweak if warranted. We'll prioritize mitigation (temporary easing of burst window and increase of per-key soft limit) while we run a config audit and postmortem.

I'll update in 30–45 minutes with next steps.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spikes in 429s and tail latency — urgent

Laura / Marissa — quick technical findings from SRE-side triage: 

> From preliminary logs and token-bucket counters we see Brightline's key exceeded the instantaneous burst allowance multiple times. The configured burst window for their tenant is 2s while the rate-adapter assumes a 10s smoothing window for that workload pattern. The adapter then dropped the request and the client retried, compounding the burst.

Root causes identified so far:
- Policy mismatch: customer-facing config for 'burst_seconds' set to 2s (likely legacy), while the runtime's pacing profiles for batched generation expect 8–12s windows for the model variant Brightline is using.
- Safety valve overlap: regional global safety valve (deploy 2026-08-30) has an aggressive headroom threshold; when combined with the above it flips from soft-fail to hard-throttle under retry storms.
- Quota vs reserve confusion: Brightline has a pooled quota and a per-key soft cap; the pooling logic didn't drop into fallback mode because the per-key cap hit first.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now (low risk):
1) Increase burst_seconds for Brightline tenant to 12s (temporary).
2) Raise per-key soft limit by 20% for 2 hours to let morning ramp pass.
3) Enable immediate fallback routing to a compatible smaller model for requests that start hitting 429s.
4) Add a temporary retry-backoff header to instruct client SDKs to back off faster if they see 429s.

I'll open SRE-789 and push a config flip; Marcus, can you approve the temporary safety-valve adjustment for us-east-1? Marissa — would appreciate exec visibility in case we need to approve extended headroom or credits.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightline.io>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Brightline production impact — ask for exec approval (credits/headroom)

Team — looping in Grace and Marcus for visibility. Brightline is a strategic mid-market account; they are experiencing user-facing degradation this morning due to the throttling pattern Karthik identified.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: please execute the SRE mitigation (burst_seconds -> 12s, soft limit +20%) and keep the window capped to 2 hours until we validate stability.
- Grace: need exec signoff on a short-term headroom increase for Brightline (up to +30% billable headroom for the month) if SRE indicates cost will spike. This is to avoid churn risk.
- Laura: liaise with Sam and confirm whether they can apply client-side backoff header by EOD; that will reduce retry storms and give SRE breathing room.

I'll prepare a one-page customer note and an offer for one month of increased headroom if the mitigation does not fully resolve issues within 24 hours. Marcus/Grace please confirm within the hour so SRE can proceed.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightline.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 15:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spikes in 429s and tail latency — suspected quota/burst policy mismatch

Sam — quick update and timeline: 

What we changed (completed):
- Increased Brightline tenant burst_seconds to 12s (temporary change).
- Raised per-key soft limit +20% for a 2-hour window; SRE kept an eye on token usage and reverted gradually.
- Enabled fallback routing to the smaller compatible variant for long requests that exceeded the new burst thresholds.
- Sent a recommended client backoff header to Brightline SDK (request-id header included).

Observations:
- 429 rate dropped from ~6% to 0.6% within 25 minutes of the mitigation.
- p99 latency returned to baseline within ~40 minutes.

Next steps (post-incident):
1) Patch customer-facing config validation to flag burst_seconds < 6s when paired with batched generation models (owner: Product, due 2026-09-21).
2) Run a joint postmortem with Brightline and publish a remedial runbook.
3) Consider a tenant-level canary for safety-valve changes to avoid global flips affecting pooled tenants (SRE project).

Attached: burst_policy_diff.patch, mitigation_runbook.pdf

We'll schedule a 30-minute wrap-up with Brightline tomorrow to review findings and confirm any billing/headroom offers. Thanks for your patience and for sending the log snippet — that made triage much faster.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
